questions.stem: The random zig-zag movement of smoke particles observed under a microscope is called
questions.explanation: Brownian motion is the irregular movement of visible particles suspended in a fluid, caused by uneven bombardment from the invisible molecules of the fluid. It is direct evidence that air molecules exist and are in constant random motion.

distractorRationale.a: Diffusion is the net spreading of particles from high to low concentration, not the jiggling of one suspended particle
distractorRationale.c: Osmosis is the movement of solvent through a semi-permeable membrane
distractorRationale.d: Effusion is the escape of a gas through a tiny hole

questions.stem: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: In a liquid the particles are still close enough for attractive forces to fix the total volume, but they are disordered and can slide past one another, so the liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.

distractorRationale.a: A solid has both a definite shape and a definite volume because its particles vibrate about fixed lattice positions
distractorRationale.c: A gas has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume; it fills any container
distractorRationale.d: Plasma is an ionised gas and, like a gas, has no definite volume

questions.stem: Which of the following substances sublimes on heating?
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride passes directly from solid to vapour on heating, then re-forms as a white solid on the cooler upper part of the tube. Iodine and solid carbon dioxide behave the same way. The vapour is actually a mixture of ammonia and hydrogen chloride that recombines on cooling.

distractorRationale.a: Sodium chloride simply melts at about 801 degrees Celsius; it does not sublime
distractorRationale.c: Copper(II) sulphate crystals lose water of crystallisation and turn white, which is dehydration rather than sublimation
distractorRationale.d: Calcium carbonate decomposes into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, a chemical change

questions.stem: Why is a gas far more compressible than a liquid?

options.text: Gas particles are smaller than liquid particles
Gas particles are much further apart, leaving large empty spaces
Gas particles attract each other more strongly

questions.explanation: Compressing a substance means reducing the space between its particles. In a gas the particles are separated by distances many times their own diameter, so there is a great deal of empty space to remove. In a liquid the particles are already touching, so there is almost nothing left to squeeze out.

distractorRationale.a: The particles are the same size in both states; only their separation changes
distractorRationale.c: Gas particles certainly have mass, which is why gases can be weighed
distractorRationale.d: Attraction between gas particles is negligible, the opposite of what is stated

questions.stem: A pure solid is heated steadily. Its temperature rises, then remains constant for several minutes before rising again. During the constant-temperature period, the heat supplied is used to

options.text: increase the average kinetic energy of the particles
overcome the forces of attraction between the particles
break the bonds inside each molecule
increase the mass of the substance

questions.explanation: During melting, energy supplied becomes latent heat of fusion. It is used to weaken and overcome the forces holding particles in the lattice rather than to speed the particles up, so the thermometer reading does not change until all the solid has melted.

distractorRationale.a: If kinetic energy were increasing, the temperature would be rising, but it is constant
distractorRationale.c: Melting is a physical change; covalent bonds inside molecules are not broken
distractorRationale.d: Mass is conserved during a change of state

questions.stem: Cotton wool soaked in concentrated ammonia solution and cotton wool soaked in concentrated hydrochloric acid are placed at opposite ends of a long glass tube. A white ring of ammonium chloride forms
questions.explanation: Ammonia has a molar mass of 17 while hydrogen chloride has a molar mass of 36.5. By Graham's law the rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass, so the lighter ammonia travels roughly 1.5 times faster and meets the hydrogen chloride closer to the acid end.

distractorRationale.a: This would only happen if the two gases had equal molar masses and so diffused at equal rates
distractorRationale.b: This reverses the rule; the faster gas covers more distance, not less
distractorRationale.d: The two gases react on meeting at a definite front, producing a ring rather than a uniform deposit

questions.stem: Condensation is the change of a gas directly into a solid.
questions.explanation: False. Condensation is the change of a gas into a liquid, which is the reverse of vaporisation. The direct change from gas to solid is called deposition, and its reverse is sublimation.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the arrangement of particles in a solid?

options.text: Particles are arranged randomly and far apart.
Particles are closely packed in a fixed position.
Particles are loosely packed and can flow.
Particles are arranged in layers that can slide over each other.

questions.explanation: In solids, particles are closely packed together in a fixed arrangement, which gives solids a definite shape and volume. This close packing restricts the movement of particles, making them vibrate in place rather than move freely.

distractorRationale.a: This describes the arrangement in gases.
distractorRationale.c: This describes the arrangement in liquids.
distractorRationale.d: This describes the arrangement in liquids, where particles can slide over each other.
